extraction_text: Markandeya narrates that Devasena's husband Skanda (also known as Kartikeya) is served by the goddess of fortune.
Six wives of the seven sages (the Krittikas/Pleiades) approach Skanda, explaining they were unjustly abandoned by their sage husbands and ask Skanda to become their son to restore their status.

relationships: Krittikas are wives of the Seven Sages

extraction_text: Skanda agrees to be their son and promises to fulfill their wishes.

relationships: Skanda becomes adoptive son of Krittikas

extraction_text: Skanda asks Indra for advice. Indra explains that Abhijit (sister of Rohini), out of jealousy to be first, went to the forest for penance, causing confusion as a star fell from the sky.
Indra states that Brahma has ordained the time for stars like Dhanishtha, with Rohini as first, making the count sufficient.
Upon hearing Indra, the Krittikas go to heaven, becoming a shining chariot-shaped constellation presided over by Agni.
Vinata tells Skanda he is her son who provides offerings and wishes to stay with him forever.
Skanda honors Vinata, allows her to stay, and promises her daughter-in-law will revere her.
A group of mothers (Matrikas) tell Skanda they are praised as mothers of the world and wish to be his mothers.

relationships: Matrikas seek to be Skanda's mothers

extraction_text: Skanda agrees to be their son and asks what he can do to please them.

relationships: Skanda becomes adoptive son of Matrikas

extraction_text: The Matrikas ask for the status of ancient world mothers, to be revered instead of them, and to have their children returned, as those mothers took their offspring with Skanda's help.

relationships: Matrikas seek to replace ancient mothers

extraction_text: Skanda says they cannot regain lost children but will grant them new children instead.

relationships: Skanda offers new children to Matrikas

extraction_text: The Matrikas ask to eat the children of the other mothers, as their protectors are different from Skanda.

relationships: Matrikas desire to consume others' children

extraction_text: Skanda grants them children but warns against their terrible desire, blessing them to protect the honorable children.
The Matrikas agree to protect the children as Skanda wishes and express desire to live with him long.
Skanda (Kartikeya) addresses the child-stealing demons, offering them immortal souls like Rudra's.
A golden, powerful man emerges from Skanda's body, becoming a child-eating demon named Skanda's Delusion (Skanda Pashmara).

attributes.supernatural_elements: Emergence from Skanda's body, demon creation

extraction_text: Various female demons are described: Vinata as a bird-demon, Putana as a female Rakshasi, Sitaputana as a fetus-stealer, Aditi as Revati, Diti as Mukhamandika.
Skanda's male and female children are described as fetus-eating demons, with the males as husbands to the females.

Other demons include Surabhi (mother of cows) ridden by a bird-demon, Sarama (mother of dogs) as a fetus-stealer, the mother of trees residing in the Kalanka tree, and Kadru entering pregnant women to eat fetuses and give birth to snakes.
The mother of Gandharvas steals fetuses causing miscarriages, the mother of Apsaras causes stillbirths, and the daughter of the blood ocean is Skanda's nurse worshipped as Rohitayani.
Arya resides in women like Rudra in men, worshipped as Skanda's mother for granting wishes.
Markandeya concludes that children are unsafe until age sixteen, and these demons are collectively called Skanda's demons.
Markandeya advises rituals like bathing, incense, offerings, and Skanda worship to appease the demons for happiness, longevity, and courage.
Markandeya prepares to describe demons that torment men over sixteen after paying homage to Mahadeva (Shiva).
Skanda satisfied the wishes of the Mothers.
Svaha approached Skanda and declared him to be her own son, then requested a boon.

attributes.relationship: Mother-son (Svaha claims Skanda as her son)

extraction_text: Svaha revealed her identity as Daksha's daughter and her lifelong love for Agni (Fire God), wishing to live with him forever.
Skanda granted Svaha's wish by decreeing that during rituals, Brahmins must first say "Svaha!" before offering oblations into the sacred fire, thus ensuring she would always be with Agni.

attributes.result: Svaha becomes eternally united with Agni through ritual invocation

extraction_text: Svaha was satisfied, became united with her husband Agni, and exchanged honors with Skanda.

attributes.relationship: Svaha and Agni become husband and wife

extraction_text: Brahma (the Creator) instructed Skanda to go to his father Rudra (the destroyer of Tripura).
Brahma explained Skanda's origin: Rudra entered Agni and Uma entered Svaha, and through their union for the world's benefit, the invincible Skanda was born.

attributes.explanation: Skanda's birth through combined essences of Rudra/Agni and Uma/Svaha

extraction_text: Brahma described how Rudra's semen, emitted into Uma's womb, splattered and created various beings: Mingiga and Mingika from mountain splatter, others in river of blood, sunlight, earth, and trees - divided into five portions.

attributes.action: Creation of beings from divine semen
attributes.result: Birth of Mingiga, Mingika, and other beings from five portions

extraction_text: The wise ones call them the various Ganas. These terrible flesh-eaters are your congregation.

attributes.description: The Ganas are described as terrible flesh-eaters who form a congregation.

extraction_text: The army (Skanda) said, "Alright!" The one with an unparalleled soul, the father's favorite, paid homage to his father Mahadeva.

attributes.relationships: Skanda is the son of Mahadeva (Shiva) and is his favorite.

extraction_text: Those who wish to acquire wealth should worship the five types of Ganas with Aroka flowers. Those who wish to be freed from diseases should also worship similarly.

attributes.purpose: Acquiring wealth and freedom from diseases.

extraction_text: Those who wish for the welfare of children should always worship the twin Rudras, Mingiga and Mingika.

attributes.description: Mingiga and Mingika are described as twin Rudras.

extraction_text: Those who desire sons should worship the divine woman born in a tree, the flesh-eating Haritika.

attributes.description: Haritika is a divine woman born in a tree and is a flesh-eater.

extraction_text: Therefore, the Pisachas (ghosts) spoken of by people are of countless varieties. Now, O King! Listen to the origin of the bells and banners.

attributes.description: The narrator shifts from describing Pisachas to telling the origin of bells and banners.

extraction_text: Airavata (the elephant) had a pair of bells named Vaijayanti. The wise Indra himself brought them and gave them to Guha (Skanda).

attributes.relationships: Indra gives bells from Airavata to Skanda.

extraction_text: One (bell) for Vishakha, the other for Skanda. The banners of Kartikeya (Skanda) and Vishakha are red.

attributes.description: Bells are given to Vishakha and Skanda; both have red banners.

extraction_text: The immensely powerful Skanda, the army god, played with the toy dolls given to him by the gods.

attributes.relationships: The gods gave toys to Skanda.

extraction_text: Surrounded by groups of Pisachas and gods, and accompanied by the goddess of fortune, he shone on the golden mountain.

attributes.description: Skanda is depicted in a glorious setting, surrounded by various beings and the goddess of fortune.

extraction_text: With this hero, the golden mountain became resplendent, as if the radiant sun were illuminating the Mandara mountain with its beautiful caves.

attributes.description: Skanda's presence makes the golden mountain shine brilliantly, compared to the sun illuminating Mandara mountain.

extraction_text: The white mountain (Himavan) became splendid with flowering Sandana groves, oleander groves, Parijata groves, rose and Ashoka groves, Kadamba thickets, as well as heavenly deer and birds.

attributes.description: The mountain is adorned with various beautiful groves, trees, deer, and birds.

extraction_text: There were groups of celestial sages and all the great sages. The clouds roared with music, like the roaring and churning ocean.

attributes.description: Sages are present, and the clouds produce musical roars resembling the ocean.

extraction_text: The heavenly Gandharvas and Apsaras danced, and the great sound of all beings rejoicing was heard.

attributes.description: Heavenly beings dance, and there is a great sound of universal joy.

extraction_text: Thus, the whole world along with Indra, on the white mountain, watched the joyous Skanda, never tiring of the sight.

attributes.description: The entire world, including Indra, watches the joyous Skanda with endless fascination.
